laws.rule: In Plitvice Lakes National Park the park's rulebook bans swimming anywhere in the park, leaving marked paths, feeding or disturbing animals, picking plants, fishing, lighting fires, camping, cycling, shouting and walking dogs off the lead.
laws.heading: Rulebook on the Protection and Preservation of the Plitvice Lakes National Park

laws.rule: Plitvice entry tickets are sold online for a set date, entrance and time slot; the park says the ticket must be shown at the chosen entrance and you can't enter before your slot.
laws.heading: Javna ustanova Nacionalni park Plitvička jezera

laws.rule: In Northern Velebit National Park, open fires are banned (fires only in marked fireplaces, which exist only at Štirovača), camping is banned outside organised campsites, walking off marked paths is banned, picking plants and fungi is banned, dogs must be on a lead, and shouting or loud music is banned. The page names no fine amounts.

layers.process: Northern Velebit National Park sells tickets online or at its entrances (Babić Siča and Alan, open 8 am to 4 pm). Every visitor needs a ticket and must keep it until leaving. The 1-day adult ticket is EUR 7 (about A$11.12 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293), 2 days EUR 10, 3 days EUR 15; discounted tickets are EUR 5, 8 and 13; an annual ticket is EUR 50; children under 6 are free. Organised group visits must be booked at least 7 days ahead and prepaid.

layers.authority: Javna ustanova Nacionalni park Sjeverni Velebit
layers.process: The park's price list sets fees for commercial video filming (EUR 700 a day), commercial photography (EUR 300 a day), and tour operators or guided activities such as birdwatching or weddings (EUR 5 per participant). Hiking, cycling or running competitions pay EUR 300 each. Contact the park for the approval process.
